title: Magnetism Final
summary: This lesson explores the fundamental properties of magnets, including their attraction to iron, the behavior of north and south poles, magnetic fields, and how compasses function using Earth's magnetic field. Students will learn how opposite poles attract and like poles repel while visualizing magnetic forces.

sections.text: Scene: A diagram showing a bar magnet with a clearly labeled north pole and south pole, surrounded by iron objects being drawn toward it. Opposite poles are shown pulling together while like poles push apart.
Scene: A visual depiction of a magnet where lines show that the magnetic field is strongest at the poles. Another diagram shows a compass utilizing Earth's magnetic field to show direction.

learning_objectives: Identify that magnets attract iron and possess a north and south pole.
Explain how opposite poles attract and like poles repel.
Describe how compasses use Earth's magnetic field to show direction.

vocabulary.definition: Objects that attract iron and have a north and south pole.
An area around a magnet where the force is strongest at the poles.
Instruments that use Earth's magnetic field to show direction.
